propositions: The gate matches field names globally as bare attribute names, allowing any same-named attribute on an unrelated config to satisfy an inert field, resulting in false negatives for fields with common names like 'enabled', 'path', 'timeout'.
A read must be resolved to its owning dataclass rather than matched against a global set of terminal attribute names to correctly detect inert config fields.

The fixed gate newly flags exactly four fields (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure), each of which has a real reader through documented indirection or plumbing exclusions.
Each newly-flagged field requires an accurate 'read-via' marker citing its actual reader or a tracking ticket, with no silent exemptions permitted to keep CI green.
Existing gate test files must be migrated from bare-name matching to owner-resolution contracts, with RED-first tests proving the old gate passes synthetic inert fields and the fixed gate fails them.
